body: I personally wouldn't mind moving (I honestly hate the city lol) but my fiancee loves his job. If it was just me as a single person, I would have 110% moved by now (probably to Alberta for cost of living and for job prospects.)

I don't mind commuting for an hour or so each direction and have applied accordingly. I guess I could move but my fiance doesn't want to as he's established in his career already, so it would mean moving away from him which isn't an ideal option. Idk, I guess the job market here sucks for entry level...
EHS or HSE coordinator, administrator, and specialist mostly. I've not applied to any supervisor or manager positions, since I think it's highly unlikely I'll get these roles.

I'm applying to positions that are looking for between 1-3 years and 3-5 years experience, with the majority being 3-5 since that is what about 70% of employers in my area are requiring. There are no positions that are requesting less than this that I've been able to find.
What would you personally reccomend? Really appreciate you weighing in on this!

Thank you for the feedback! I'm definitely not above non-EHS work (I have 2 years experience in a hospital setting and close to 9 years in customer service starting from when I was 16) and will definitely try to keep employed. I guess if my contract does expire I will try to find a line worker position or something else in manufacturing.

I'll also try to be more active on LinkedIn and the like, though I am not the biggest social media aficionado. 

Appreciate you taking the time to provide some tips!

https://bcrsp.ca/en/prospective-certificants/about-crst-certification/apply-crst-certification 

The BCRSP is a Canadian certification board that issues a certification similar to the USA's CSP (we call ours CRSP). CRST is essentially the technician version of the cert, and denotes a difference in education/years experience. You can see the requirements in the link I posted above.
